text: A blinded comparison of three independent laboratories using PPMI CSF samples reported sensitivities of 86–96% and specificities of 93–100%, demonstrating reproducibility in expert laboratories despite methodological differences. (low confidence)
keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

text: The 2025 biomatrix meta-analysis reported pooled blood SAA sensitivity of 0.90 (95% CI 0.86–0.93) and specificity of 0.91 (0.86–0.95); these pooled estimates are limited by aggregate data, publication bias and heterogeneous studies, and do not establish a universal blood-test performance. (low confidence)
keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

text: In an analysis of PPMI and Tübingen cohort data, baseline SAA time-to-threshold predicted cognitive decline in both PPMI (hazard ratio 2·36, 95% CI 1·60–3·46) and Tübingen (2·17, 1·07–4·41), and was associated with cognitive decline in an Alzheimer-biomarker-negative PPMI subgroup. This was an observational prognostic association. (low confidence)

text: NfL interpretation needs covariate adjustment: the head-to-head study found associations with age in both CSF and plasma, and with body mass index, estimated glomerular filtration rate and chronic kidney disease in plasma. (low confidence)

text: The FDA’s August 19, 2024 Letter of Support recommends CSF SAA as a susceptibility/risk biomarker for trial enrichment and supports binary SAA assessment for selection into trials targeting common synuclein biology; its stated context is drug development and clinical trials. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-08-19)

text: A Viewpoint cautions against premature adoption of the alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay as a Parkinson disease biomarker test in general neurology practice; this is an attributed clinical-implementation caution. (low confidence)

text: Neurofilament light chain can be measured in CSF and plasma as a marker of axonal damage; higher levels have been associated with poorer cognitive outcomes in Parkinson disease, but it is nonspecific and also rises with age and other inflammatory or degenerative conditions. (low confidence)

text: In the 2023 cross-sectional PPMI study, CSF SAA sensitivity for clinically diagnosed Parkinson disease was 87·7% (95% CI 84·9–90·5) and specificity against healthy controls was 96·3% (93·4–99·2); these estimates describe that study population rather than general-population screening. (low confidence)
keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

text: SAA positivity is heterogeneous: in the 2023 PPMI study, sensitivity in sporadic Parkinson disease with olfactory deficit was 98·6%, compared with 78·3% without olfactory deficit. A negative result therefore cannot universally exclude clinically diagnosed Parkinson disease. (low confidence)
keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

text: NfL is a marker of neuroaxonal injury that can complement alpha-synuclein SAA, rather than directly measuring alpha-synuclein seeds. (low confidence)

text: In the 2025 head-to-head NfL study, CSF assays discriminated Parkinson’s disease from atypical parkinsonian disorders more accurately than plasma assays (AUC 0.966–0.974 versus 0.917–0.924); combining CSF NfL with alpha-synuclein RT-QuIC improved accuracy in that cohort. (low confidence)
keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

text: The 2024 Zarkali review reports associations of baseline CSF Alzheimer-related biomarkers—higher phosphorylated tau, lower amyloid-beta 42, and lower amyloid-beta 42/total tau ratio—with worsening motor and cognitive performance at follow-up; these characterize co-pathology and prognosis rather than alpha-synuclein seeding itself. (low confidence)
keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

text: In a blinded 30-site cross-sectional study, skin biopsy detected cutaneous phosphorylated alpha-synuclein in 92.7% (89 of 96) of patients with PD, 98.2% (54 of 55) with MSA, 96.0% (48 of 50) with DLB and 100% (22 of 22) with pure autonomic failure, versus 3.3% (4 of 120) of controls; the authors state that further research in unselected clinical populations is needed to externally validate the findings. (low confidence)
keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

text: Alpha-synuclein SAA detects seeding-competent misfolded aggregates by amplifying their ability to template recombinant alpha-synuclein aggregation; thioflavin T fluorescence detects the resulting fibrils. RT-QuIC and PMCA are related SAA approaches. (high confidence)

text: Expert-laboratory concordance does not remove the need for assay standardization: protocol heterogeneity, recombinant substrate, buffers, beads, shaking, temperature, and preanalytical handling affect comparability. (high confidence)
keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

text: Blood alpha-synuclein assays require control of peripheral contamination and sample handling: erythrocytes and platelets contribute alpha-synuclein, and hemolysis and storage conditions can vary results. CSF SAA also requires preanalytical controls, including blood contamination and freeze-thaw handling. (high confidence)
keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

text: SAA seeding activity and total CSF alpha-synuclein concentration are different measurements: the 2024 Zarkali review found that total CSF alpha-synuclein did not show a consistent relationship with Lewy body pathology or longitudinal motor or cognitive change. (low confidence)
keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

text: Longitudinal prognostic results differ by analysis: a PPMI analysis found no statistically significant association between baseline seeding measures and progression among manifest patients, whereas a separate analysis associated baseline time-to-threshold with subsequent cognitive decline in PPMI and an independent Tübingen cohort. Diagnostic positivity should not be treated as an established general progression measure. (medium confidence)
keywords: Alpha-synuclein seed amplification assay and fluid biomarkers

text: CSF sampling is relatively invasive, motivating SAA studies in other specimens. The 2024 Zarkali review describes promising skin-biopsy results and lower accuracy with olfactory-mucosa sampling; performance should be interpreted for the specimen and assay actually tested. (low confidence)
